items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mode gets brand new trailer showing promising results
items.summary: This has come along so well!
items.content:
CyberMP is a project that shows great promise within the Cyberpunk 2077 community.

Development on CyberMP, the fan-made multiplayer mod for Cyberpunk 2077 , seems to be coming along well if a new short video is to be believed.

CyberMP is a mod that we reported on last year after seeing a few short glimpses of what multiplayer within Cyberpunk 2077 ’s Night City would look like.

Although the project was still early on, its developers seemed keen to keep working at it, coming up with some bright ideas to keep the project fresh and exciting.

A new video uploaded to the CyberMP YouTube channel has demonstrated the multiplayer mod in action, showing a series of clips taken from a recent playtest session in which around ten users or so were playing together in the same game instance.

We first get to see all the players gathered together in the Eastern Badlands part of the map overlooking Night City, before the video cuts to a race in the city in which every player is competing against each other.

After that, we see clips of players sharing a four-seat vehicle together, followed by the entire server gathered in Lizzie’s Bar, and then a bunch of players racing in vehicles across the bridge.

The video ends with a demonstration of what combat looks like, showing players using grenades to blow each other up.

Take a look for yourself with the embedded video below.

Read More: Cyberpunk 2077 gamer stuns with 'all cyber, no punk' playthrough

On the whole, it looks like the mod is coming along nicely. While there are still a few parts that are rough around the edges, it seems like the mod functions pretty well when under a heavy server load.

There are still some glitches, but on the whole it seems that the CyberMP team’s stress test went successfully.

“As you know, we recently held our second semi-open test — we selected testers from applications and ran testing for 2 days!” reads a message on the CyberMP Discord server.

According to the team, the peak number of concurrent players on the same server reached 66 people, a new record for them. However, this also led to the server becoming increasingly unstable as more players flooded in.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Multiplayer is Evolving - Modders Show Gameplay and Discuss Progress
items.content:
1 10 Aug 21:28 CD Projekt RED presented an interesting story in Cyberpunk 2077, but some gamers wanted not only a single-player game mode but also something like GTA Online. A similar multiplayer project is being attempted by the modding community.

In August, the creators of the "CyberMP" project once again reminded about themselves and presented a new trailer with gameplay footage. They also shared the results of their testing. According to the developers, with 30-40 people online, the server worked stably:

The peak online was 66 people on one server – this is a record for us! Unfortunately, with a larger influx of players, the server started to work less stably, but thanks to the tests, we found the causes of the errors [...]

The project is not yet perfect: the authors of CyberMP identified "many small bugs and errors," some of which have already been fixed. The modders also noted that while they were preparing the post with the test results, they managed to refine the stress test tools, and the problem with a large number of connections has already been resolved.

Currently, CD Projekt RED is developing a sequel to Cyberpunk 2077 – the project does not yet have a release date.

items.title: I have FOMO for the worst era of Cyberpunk 2077
items.summary: Bring gear stats and ripperdoc-specific cyberware back to the RPG
items.content:
Bring gear stats and ripperdoc-specific cyberware back to the RPG's sequel!

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: CD Projekt Red) Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A few months after Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty launched alongside v2.0, I stepped into Night City for the very first time . The experience was baffling. If I wasn't puzzling over the different kinds of operating systems and playstyles, I was getting an eyeful of every townie's butt cheeks as they strutted about Watson looking like randomized Sims. I powered through the weirdness and learned to embrace it, going on to complete it three times in less than six months.

Anything I didn't understand was chalked up to being a newbie. The lack of handholding or mechanic explanations confounded me at first, but I reminded myself that I was playing a three-year-old RPG for the first time. Maybe developer CD Projekt Red saw no need to tutorialize it too much for the hordes of returning fans, I wondered?

Only now, on my fifth playthrough, has curiosity finally gotten the better of me. One YouTube rabbit hole later thanks to videos like this , I've been confronted with how incredibly different this game was at launch. Not just in terms of being far more stable and less prone to bugs and crashes these days, but in the evolution of some pretty interesting mechanics and systems that I honestly wish I'd gotten to experience for myself. Cyberpunk 2, take note please.

I bounced off of Cyberpunk 2077 for 2 months when I first played it, and that makes it perfect for Xbox Game Pass

I adore games that let me diva out . I want to be the most dripped-out baddie in the Badlands, so it makes sense that one of my biggest draws into the world of Cyberpunk 2077 was V's impressive wardrobe. I made it my mission from day-one to traverse every nook and cranny of Night City in search of the coolest threads V could lay her chromed-out hands on, and for the most part, I succeeded. One thing I shrugged off on my hunt for sartorial supremacy was the fact that clothing items, much like weapons or cyberware, are color-coded into tier grades. In the end I'd just assumed it was a Night City classist thing; grey tier-one gear was simply the cheap bargain bin stuff I'd start out with, while orange tier 5 pieces might run me a few more eddies in exchange for looking like street punk royalty. It wasn't until I finally took it upon myself to research why clothing items are tiered despite only being cosmetics that I started to feel left out.

Surprise, surprise: the color-coded tier levels on clothing items in Cyberpunk 2077 are a vestige from a time when they did serve a greater purpose. Once upon a time, gear could be crafted out of tiered parts just like quickhacks, weapons, and grenades, granting V different buffs and armor values depending on the tier level. They even had mod slots!

Cyberpunk 2077 has finally made me the corpo baddie of my RPG dreams and I regret everything already Six years later, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners season 2 wraps gaming's greatest comeback story With no combat system, Zero Parades is an RPG all about skill checks and spycraft, and it's more exciting for it

This resulted in some truly, uh, interesting fashion choices as players sought to min-max the hell out of their gear (as you can see from the vintage screenshot above, circa-2021). Transmog didn't exist at all, so it was perfectly acceptable to slink into a stealthy thief gig dressed to the nines in stilettos, a polka dot bra, and a hideous fluorescent beanie.

Suddenly, it all made sense. I feel highly privileged to be playing a version of the game that looks and feels fantastic, but there's something fittingly absurd about mercs cutting about Corpo Plaza like a half-dressed Barbie doll found in a dumpster. Sometimes I feel bad for being the only fashionable person in Night City as it is; how could these commoners possibly compete with Queen V's perfectly coordinated red, black, and gold outfits? But in another life, I, too, was meant to be clad in mesh vests and office slacks. Maybe I'm the weird one for sticking out like a sore thumb after all.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

This is not me championing for CDPR to bring back a transmog-less world in Cyberpunk 2077. I'd sooner zero myself than let Judy see me in stained sneakers. But I do wonder how it would have felt to play the game relying on my gear to actually power me up rather than adding yet more weight and importance to the ever-grindy path of cyberware leveling instead.

It's too easy to be the most chromed out queen this side of the Blackwall, let alone the best-dressed merc.

items.title: The new CyberPunk 2077 game is more analogue than you might think
items.summary: You might want to get on board.
items.content:
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: CD Projekt Red) Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter If you're a fan of CD Projekt Red's Cyberpunk 2077, you might have been excited about some of the headlines appearing in the past couple of days. 'New Cyberpunk 2077 game reveals official gameplay,' one read. ‘Cyberpunk 2077 returns with ambitious new release,' was another. One even suggested that a new Cyberpunk 2077 was going to steal GTA 6's thunder.

Alas, some fans might have been disappointed to read those stories and discover that the new game is more analogue than what they might have imagined. Given how long it takes to make an AAA video game, it was highly unlikely that we would get Cyberpunk 2077 2 in 2027 – 2028 maybe, but even that's a very optimistic estimate.

The new Cyberpunk 2077 is, in fact, a board game. But don't write it off, it follows in a long traditional of video game to board game transitions, and some of them have been quite good.

Watch On Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game looks set to do justice to the video game's vast lore and worldbuilding in its physical scale. The eight-minute unboxing video above reveals just how huge it is with the various miniatures, mission cards, character boards and gameplay expansions

Published by Go On Board, it's billed as a cooperative, story-driven campaign game. Players take on the roles of Edgerunners, exploring Night City and completing 13 multi-stage missions. A timer mechanic is intended to replicate the paced of the action of the video game.

Board of Prime Day?! There's a board game for that GTA 6 could be the final death knell for physical media Hear me out, GTA 6's graphics might be too good The game follows the release of the trading card game Cyberpunk TCG. If its successful, it should be able to evolve alongside the video game franchise for many years.

The trend of turning video games into board games has exploded over the past decade, with crowdfunding platforms like Kickstarter or Gamefound playing a big role in helping the physical adaptations get off the ground. They also tap into the growing interest in physical media and analogue tech as a respite from digital screen time, providing a physical social experience.

Critical reception has been a bit of a mixed bag. Some have been heralded as masterpieces, others are criticised as overpriced miniature-fests that prioritise plastic over playable design.

The most successful adaptations are those that don't just copy-paste the digital game, but translate its feeling and core loops into smart, physical mechanics. Slay the Spire: The Board Game is much loved for how it turned a single-player digital roguelike and turning it into cooperative tabletop deck-builder, and Frostpunk succeeded in bringing the punishing decision-making of digital survival games to the table.

On a very different note, the cosy Dorfromantik: The Board Game captured the zen-like puzzle game vibe of its digital counterpart.

How Cyberpunk 2077 accidentally inspired this gorgeous anime football platformer Fans want to send this new Stranger Things spin-off back to the Upside Down How one video game brought me back to gaming after 15 years On the other hand, Dark Souls: The Board Game was seen by some as being tedious and repetitive despite its gorgeous miniatures.

Board games can also be the ultimate collector's item for video game fans. Even if a $200 Elden Ring or Resident Evil board games only hits the table once or twice a year, the gorgeous, highly detailed miniatures also serve as display pieces.

You can find out more about Cyberpunk 2077 The Board Game on the Go On Board website.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Is Coming to Xbox Game Pass
items.summary: CD PROJEKT RED announces that its open-world role-playing game Cyberpunk 2077 will join Xbox Game Pass Premium and Ultimate on March 10. Snapshot: Cyberpunk 2077 will soon be available on Xbox Game Pass, joining CD
items.content:
CD PROJEKT RED announces that its open-world role-playing game Cyberpunk 2077 will join Xbox Game Pass Premium and Ultimate on March 10.

Starting March 10, players can enter the dark future with Cyberpunk 2077 and take on the role of Night City mercenary V — a fully customizable character enhanced with cybernetic implants. Players will embark on a once-in-a-lifetime heist to steal an experimental prototype known as the “Relic” — and watch the trajectory of V’s life change when things don’t go as planned.

What follows is a narratively-rich open-world experience where every decision matters, as players’ choices affect how the story unfolds. Robust perk trees, futuristic cyberware, and a range of powerful weapons — from thermal katanas to talking guns — are all at players’ disposal to build their ultimate playstyle and define their legend.

Cyberpunk 2077 on Xbox Series X|S comes with every update released for the game since launch, which brought myriad technical improvements, new features, and additional content such as quests, vehicles, and character customization options. Players on Xbox Series X can also play Cyberpunk 2077 at 60 frames per second in Performance Mode or with 4K Ultra HD visuals in Quality Mode. Players on Xbox One will receive Cyberpunk 2077 and everything released up to and including Update 1.6 — the Edgeruners Update.

Cyberpunk 2077 joins Xbox Game Pass Premium and Ultimate for both Xbox Series X|S and Xbox One consoles on March 10.

For more information about the game, visit cyberpunk.net and follow the game on Facebook , X , and Instagram .

items.title: Five Years Of ‘Cyberpunk 2077,’ My Favorite Game Of All Time
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2077 is my favorite game of all time, and as it celebrates five years since release, I reflect on what it meant to me.
items.content:
Gaming Five Years Of ‘Cyberpunk 2077,’ My Favorite Game Of All Time By Paul Tassi ,

Forbes contributors publish independent expert analyses and insights. News and opinion about video games, television, movies and the internet. Follow Author Dec 11, 2025, 10:24am EST Cyberpunk 2077 CDPR “What’s your favorite game?” It’s a simple question that you would imagine someone who writes about video games for a living would have an answer to. But it’s always been a tough one. Halo 3 ? Maybe Mass Effect 2 ? Super Smash Bros. 64 ? Destiny 2, the game I’ve sunk 5,000 hours into?

I never had a clear answer until a few years ago, when I suddenly realized that after four playthroughs and hundreds of hours, it was Cyberpunk 2077 , which just celebrated its fifth anniversary this week.

It feels improbable. I loved The Witcher 3 , which was my first experience with CDPR, and as such, I was interested in Cyberpunk 2077 , albeit perhaps with less enthusiasm than some. But the game was released and consumed by one of the wildest launch stories ever, a disastrous release of an unbaked game mired with technical issues to the point where it was actually delisted from the PlayStation store for months, something almost never seen in the industry. It was broken broken.

Well, for some. Sure, I had bugs on PC in those early days, and performance could have been better, but it was certainly better than running it on console. And if you could block out the noise of the larger controversies, you could see it. You could see the core of this game was great, and if it had fixed things, added things, delivered on its full potential, it could have been great.

Cyberpunk 2077 CDPR Play Puzzles & Games on Forbes FEATURED | Frase By Forbes ™

It is great, now. CDPR spent at least two years getting the game to where it should have been at launch, but in the five-year span, it has dramatically overhauled most major systems in the game, particularly its skill trees. It also then released Phantom Liberty, where at that point, I was not all that surprised it became my favorite DLC of all time, as well.

Cyberpunk 2077 is simply best in class across so many categories. Night City is one of the best realized environments I’ve ever seen across any open world title, beating out Grand Theft Auto handily in terms of a gorgeous, living space (that got more convincing with patches to civilians and traffic, in time).

The voicework here is stellar. Yes, the star feature was Keanu Reeves, but there is no question in my mind that Cherami Leigh’s V is the best first-person narrator I’ve seen in a game. The concept of every bit of the game, even cutscenes, taking place in first person only worked because of her (and Male V, Gavin Drea, was solid as well). Leigh’s performance, however praised, was not praised enough.

The excellent voicework extends to the excellent characters and the writing to bring them to life. In particular, Judy and Panam quickly became some of my favorite video game NPCs, with Panam in particular being an unforgettable love interest that would make Mass Effect and Baldur’s Gate players jealous. Even if she rejected me. How many NPCs have ever broken your heart?

Cyberpunk 2077 CDPR None of this would work if the game itself was not fun. It was solid enough to start, but when Cyberpunk 2077 really kicked into gear was after its major skills overhaul. Half the reason I made four(!) different Vs was not just to make different story decisions, but to commit to different pathways and builds. I had my pure melee build (stupidly overpowered), my run and gun shotgun, LMG tank build, my hacking-only build full of exploding heads and cyberpsychosis, and finally, my final and favorite run, throwing knives only, like some sort of Goldeneye modifier. I don’t think there’s a better metaphor for Cyberpunk’s transformation than the original throwing knife skill being throwing a literal, single knife in your inventory, then needing to find it afterward lest you lose it. After the grand skill tree rework patch, it was switched to being a cooldown with infinite ammo, and it ended up being one of the most hilarious, legitimately strong builds in the game thanks to CDPR investing in the idea, rather than abandoning it.

Again, I made four Vs for four full runs of the game, at least until I was told to meet Hanako at Embers, as I’d done most of the endings by that point already. I have never done that many playthroughs of a single-player game before, and none of them felt like a slog. Ultimately I made my way to a new, “true," ending in Phantom Liberty which was one of the most gut-wrenching sequences I can remember in a game.

Something happened midway through these five years that changed my perception of all this. After blacking out, falling and smacking my head a number of times, I was diagnosed with epilepsy in my 30s, a rarity. Now, every time V’s brain glitched out because of the relic, and she found herself going dark and hitting the floor, I could feel that kind of pain and confusing. She was marching toward her death, I am not (well, technically I could die from one of these), but there is something to be said here about how Cyberpunk deals with grief and bravery in the face of illness (read my friend Gene Park’s essay about how he connected to Cyberpunk via his own cancer diagnosis).

Cyberpunk 2077 CDPR There is still lost potential in Cyberpunk . The idea of three different lifepaths never really manifested. The romance options, while compelling, are locked and limited. Johnny can be…a lot, if you ask me. But no game is perfect. Where it shines, it doesn’t just shine, it stands up to the greats in video game history and as such, is a great itself. For me, the greatest.

items.summary: Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live! This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below: Vehicles Updated Aut
items.content:
Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live!

This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below:

Vehicles

  • Updated AutoDrive. When driving to a selected point, the vehicle now drives smoothly, overtakes blocking vehicles and no longer stops at traffic lights. Free Roam mode has also been upgraded to follow traffic rules and navigate the city more reliably.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Johnny always spawned in the passenger seat when using the Delamain Cab service.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where applying CrystalCoat to the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru caused its wheels to flash in different colors.

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Most of the new poses introduced in Update 2.3 now work with any gender.

    [/*]

  • Disabled NPC collision, which will make it easier to position NPCs on top of other objects with collision (e.g. on car hoods).

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where some of the poses didn't work for Royce.

    [/*]

Quests & Open World

  • Freedom - Fixed the journal entry that appears when the player chooses not to steal the Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred."

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where, after V fails to pursue and stop Semimaru and receives a text from River saying he'll contact V soon, the follow-up message never arrives.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where the Yaiba Semimaru could flip over during the chase, preventing the player from entering it.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - It's no longer possible to trigger the quest if River died during The Hunt.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Players can now acquire the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru through AUTOFIXER even if they failed The Hunt, which normally unlocks the side quest where the vehicle is obtained.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed a game crash that could occur in certain circumstances after leaving the Yaiba showroom event.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed an issue where the proxy interface UI in the Yaiba showroom is cut off when the "Larger HUD Elements" setting is enabled.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Fixed several localization and lipsync issues in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle to disable vignette. It can be found in Settings → Graphics → Basic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on PC and Mac where Ray-Traced Reflections might not display correctly when enabled under certain conditions.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several issues with displaying text messages from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Various fixes for fluff vendors.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Fixed an issue where NVIDIA Reflex could be disabled while DLSS Frame Generation was enabled, causing the screen to turn pink.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Path Tracing didn't activate properly in certain scenarios.

    [/*]

Mac-specific

  • Fixed an issue where changing graphics presets on Mac set Screen Space Reflections to a higher setting compared to the equivalent presets on PC.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing a permanent white screen when Frame Generation is enabled while entering the braindance in The Information.

    [/*]

  • Selecting "Defaults" in Video Settings no longer turns HDR Mode off.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where setting the MetalFX DRS Maximum Resolution above the value applied by the “For this Mac” preset could cause visual artifacts.

    [/*]

  • Fixed the inverted behavior of the "Mute Game in Background" toggle in Settings.

    [/*]

  • Removed the outdated "(Requires Game Restart)" disclaimer from the mouseover description of the "Disable Spatial Audio" setting.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on the App Store version that caused the game to become stuck on the “Press Space to continue” breaching screen.

    [/*]

  • Various stability and performance optimizations.

    [/*]

Update 2.3 lands tomorrow!

Experience Night City in a whole new way — this patch introduces 4 new vehicles, the AutoDrive feature, self-driving Delamain cabs and more! Vehicles
